# Biff 2.0.4: LLM skills

Jacob O'Bryant | 25 Oct 2026

I've just released Biff v2.0.4 . This release has a hodge-podge of tweaks and fixes based on my own usage . There is also one big addition: a set of LLM skills. From the starter project's README:

> biff-spec-review : reads spec/ and generates a plan to implement it. biff-spec-dev : implements the plan generated by biff-spec-dev . Calls biff-code-review afterward. biff-code-review : reviews recent code changes against a list of Biff-specific coding conventions. Invoked by biff-spec-dev automatically, or you can run it manually. biff-code-quality : instructions the agent to run clojure -M:run code-quality and fix any test/lint failures. biff-dev : instructions for using the REPL. Invoked by agents automatically when they write Clojure code.

- biff-spec-review : reads spec/ and generates a plan to implement it.

- biff-spec-dev : implements the plan generated by biff-spec-dev . Calls biff-code-review afterward.

- biff-code-review : reviews recent code changes against a list of Biff-specific coding conventions. Invoked by biff-spec-dev automatically, or you can run it manually.

- biff-code-quality : instructions the agent to run clojure -M:run code-quality and fix any test/lint failures.

- biff-dev : instructions for using the REPL. Invoked by agents automatically when they write Clojure code.

After upgrading your biff.tasks dependency to 2.0.4 , these skills will be synced to your local project whenever you run clj -M:run dev .

The most important skill here is biff-code-review . It contains a list of rules for writing code that conforms to Biff conventions. The rules are the result of my own painstaking review of reams of crappy LLM-generated Biff code. From testing them out on a fresh project, I'm fairly pleased with the result. The code I've gotten is definitely still a little weird in places, but it's crossed the "good enough" threshold.

My general flow for making Biff apps is now:

- Start a new project .

- Edit the spec/README.md file.

- Run biff-spec-review and then biff-spec-dev (the latter of which calls biff-code-review ).

Sometimes I'll use a fancy model to review specs/code and a dumber model to do the implementation.

I had some trouble figuring out a structure for getting LLMs to actually follow my rules. I've had success with this flow:

- I try to phrase each rule so it's very explicit/unambiguous/black and white. Either the rule is violated or it's not.

- biff-code-review instructs the LLM to copy a checklist for all the rules into your project. The LLM goes through your code and adds a bullet point (with filename and line numbers) to the checklist file whenever it finds a violation. After the code review, any checklist items without violations are checked off.

- The LLM then goes through the checklist and applies fixes.

I structured this in a way so that if needed you can do a human-in-the-loop thing: you can edit the checklist before step 3 starts to add any violations the LLM may have missed. During step 3, the LLM doesn't edit the checklist file, so you can manually mark off/not mark off items and then redo step 3.
